newsitem.title: USA: O'Sullivan sees stronger Q2 net income.
newsitem.headline: O'Sullivan sees stronger Q2 net income.

text.p: O'Sullivan Industries Holdings Inc said Monday that net income for its fiscal second quarter is estimated to be 25 percent to 35 percent higher than its fiscal first quarter's, on slightly lower net sales.

Net income for the first quarter ended September 30 was $3.5 million, or $0.21 a share, on sales of $83.1 million. In the second quarter of fiscal 1996, net income was $458,000, or $0.03 a share, on net sales of $79.6 million.
O'Sullivan, which makes ready-to-assemble furniture, said its projection for second quarter earnings was based on stronger than anticipated gross margins.

"We are enjoying strong gross margins this quarter due to improved product mix from innovative new products, such as the Cockpit, that has increased average selling prices," Daniel O'Sullivan, chairman, said in a statement. "We are controlling our overhead and related expenses and are continuing to experience high capacity utilization at all three plants.
He said sales for the quarter are less than originally planned due to the bankruptcy and current liquidation of a major customer.
The loss of those sales was partially offset by orders from existing customers, as well as new customers such as two major home improvement retailers.
In the 1996 fiscal second quarter, the bankrupt customer accounted for approximately $7.5 million in net sales, O'Sullivan said.
